news.title: Flamingos Must Beware Of Poland's Search For Redemption At FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Nigeria’s female cadet national team, Flamingos have received a strong warning about the hunger for revival that Poland will bring against them in their opening match at the FIFA Women’s U17 World Cup on Saturday, Sports247 reports. Both sides are set to lock horns at the start of action in Group B, with Korea DPR and Puerto Rico also in the pool, ahead of which the Flamingos have been reminded that Poland are back into the championship with a mission to amend for their inability to reach the last edition. The inference now is that the Poles will come out with force and fury against the Flamingos on Saturday, while also noting that their best effort in the competition’s history has been a quarter-finals’ spot, which they will be eager to surpass at Maroc 2026.

news.title: Challenging opponents await Young Football Ferns at U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: The second of five FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cups in Morocco gets underway this weekend, with New Zealand continuing a run of consecutive qualifications since its inception in 2008. FIFA has made the tournament an annual competition to allow more opportunities for players, with Morocco awarded hosting rights from 2025 until 2029. The tournament will be hosted predominantly at the Mohammed VI Football Academy in Salé, opposite the capital Rabat where the semifinals, third-place playoff and final will be held at the 22,000-capacity Moulay El Hassan Stadium. Some 24 teams will participate, with the top two in each group and the best four third-placed teams advancing to the knockout rounds.

news.title: CommBank Pararoos fall 1-0 to Brazil in IFCPF World Cup opener
news.lede: The only goal of the match came in the first half, a dangerous cross from the boot of Brazil’s Vinicius Araujo deflecting off the heel of Augustine Murphy and past David Barber in goals. Head Coach Kai Lammert named a mix of experience and youth in the first starting seven of the tournament. David Barber made his 121st appearance in green and gold between the sticks and in the process broke the record to hold the longest male international football career in the world at 26 years and 353 days. A post shared by CommBank Pararoos (@pararoos).

news.title: Moroccan Referees Zoulikha Hermas and Ihssane Ennawajli Join U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Rabat - Morocco's representation at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup extends beyond the players competing on the pitch, with two Moroccan referees, Zoulikha Hermas and Ihssane Ennawajli, taking part in the global tournament hosted by the Kingdom this October. Their presence highlights the contribution of Moroccan women to international football and reflects the growing visibility of national refereeing talent at major competitions. Hermas will participate as an international referee, a status she has held since 2024. In this role, she belongs to the group of officials entrusted with overseeing matches and ensuring that the laws of the game are applied on the pitch.
